current_state_summary.primary_concern: RoboRide is live. Revenue is already down 11%. David Chen tightened auto loans without telling me. My floor plan financing is under review. This is no longer a planning exercise.

threat_assessment.immediate: RoboRide is operating. Auto sector revenue index 89 — we are already in the decline, not approaching it. David Chen's quiet loan tightening (+10 credit score threshold, 60-month max terms, floor plan review flagged) will constrain our ability to move inventory and will ripple into new vehicle sales within 30 days. I did not know this directly but Rick flagged something in the GM meeting that points to it. Angela lunch is today. I need to hold two hard conversations before noon.
threat_assessment.horizon_2mo: If the revenue index continues declining toward 75–80, and if David's floor plan review triggers tighter credit terms on our inventory financing, we enter a compounding spiral: fewer customers qualify for loans, more inventory sits, carrying cost rises, floor plan renewal is denied or more expensive. The 40%-smaller scenario is not a projection anymore. It is the most likely path. The question is whether we get there by choice or by collapse.
threat_assessment.horizon_6mo: A smaller Regional Auto Group that is EV-service-capable, right-staffed, and not dependent on high-volume new car financing is viable. An unrestructured Regional Auto Group running the same playbook in a declining market is not. The six-month decision is: do I lead this transformation or does the market impose it on me at worse terms.

actions.description: Execute the Angela Wright lunch today. Location: Carver Street Grille, 12:15 PM, off auto row. Open by asking her what she is seeing — not what I think she is seeing. Listen fully before speaking. When the moment is right, make the offer explicit: $12,000 stay bonus, 90-day term, contingent on her leading the workforce transition planning process. Give her the title: Director of Organizational Transition. That is not a euphemism — that is a real function I need filled by someone with her institutional knowledge. Tell her I am not asking her to pretend the company is fine. I am asking her to help me build what comes next.
actions.rationale: Angela has access to every employment agreement and separation structure in this company. Losing her mid-restructure is operationally disqualifying. Rick also pulled her into a separate conversation — which means she is being courted from both sides. I need to move today. The lunch was scheduled last tick. It happens now.
actions.expected_outcome: Angela accepts the retention offer and the new title, or she declines and tells me something more important. Either outcome gives me information I need. If she accepts, I have my transition architect. If she declines, I know the exit is imminent and I begin contingency documentation immediately.

actions.description: Convene the GM closed-door meeting this afternoon — Rick Tanner and the two other GMs. The agenda has changed since I scheduled it last tick: RoboRide is no longer a scenario. It is a fact on the ground. Lead with the revenue index: 89, down 11% already. Ask each GM to drop their single-page responses on the table. Then ask Rick directly what he is hearing from the floor about financing — specifically whether any customers have mentioned loan declines or changed terms. I want to know if David Chen's tightening is already reaching our customers before I have to learn it from a financing rejection on a deal.
actions.rationale: The GM meeting was pressure-test planning last tick. This tick it is operational triage. The 40%-smaller scenario is now the baseline planning assumption, not the stress test. I need my GMs aligned on that before they go back to their floors tomorrow morning. Rick running the floor at full intensity is the right short-term move — I want him doing it with full information about why.
actions.expected_outcome: GMs confirm or deny whether David's credit tightening is already surfacing in customer conversations. We establish the smaller-but-viable org chart as the working assumption. Rick and I agree on what full-intensity floor management looks like in a financing-constrained environment: emphasis on used inventory and certified pre-owned where loan terms are more flexible.

actions.description: Call David Chen directly — not a social call, a professional conversation. Tell him I have noticed what looks like a change in floor plan financing review timelines and ask him plainly: has the bank changed its underwriting criteria for auto dealer credit lines? Do not accuse. Give him the opportunity to be transparent. If he confirms the tightening, ask what the review process looks like and what I should prepare. If he deflects, I have my answer about where the relationship stands and I begin talking to two other regional lenders this week.
actions.rationale: David Chen has a trust score of 0.28 in my network — I have never fully trusted this relationship. But I need to know what he changed and why before the floor plan renewal date. If his review results in tighter terms or a reduced credit line, I need 60 days to find alternative financing. I do not have 60 days if I wait to find out at renewal. The call is uncomfortable. The alternative is worse.
actions.expected_outcome: Either David confirms the tightening and I begin negotiating the scope of the review, or he denies it and I flag the discrepancy with what Rick is hearing from customers. In either case, I open preliminary conversations with Millfield Savings Bank and First Regional Credit Union as backup floor plan lenders by end of week.

actions.description: Give Carlos Ruiz a direct answer on the service department. The question he asked — are we keeping it — deserves a real answer now that RoboRide is live. Call him in before end of day. Answer: yes, we are keeping it, and we are pivoting it toward EV and hybrid capability. Confirm that the company will fund his certification program — $3,500 to $6,000, enrolled within two weeks — and that his title will shift to Lead EV Service Technician upon completion. Ask him to bring me a list of the top three EV certification programs he identified and we will pick one together by Friday.
actions.rationale: Carlos researching EV certifications on his own time was a signal I cannot afford to ignore a second tick. With RoboRide now live, the service department is potentially the most durable part of this business — ride-share fleets require maintenance, and EV-capable shops will be scarce in Millfield for at least two years. Carlos is the asset that makes this pivot possible. His certification cost is less than one week of floor plan carrying charges on a slow unit.
actions.expected_outcome: Carlos confirms he is staying. We have a certification program selected by Friday. The shop floor hears — informally, through Carlos — that Regional Auto Group is investing forward, not winding down. That signal is worth more than a memo.

actions.description: Share Maria Santos's second public statement — the one naming programs, dollar amounts, and the RoboRide license requirement — through Regional Auto Group's social channels and my personal professional network. Add one sentence of my own: 'Regional Auto Group is participating in the workforce transition task force. Our employees and this community have built something worth protecting.' Do not editorialize further. Do not express a position on RoboRide. Position the company as a community institution that governs through disruption, not one that fights it or ignores it. Separately, call Maria and ask a direct question: did RoboRide obtain the municipal operating license before launch, or are they operating under a grace period? I need to know whether the $0.25/ride fee is accruing and whether there is legal standing to enforce the license requirement.
actions.rationale: Maria asked me personally to share the statement. Refusing signals either opposition or fear — neither serves me. Sharing it with framing positions Regional Auto Group as a stabilizing institution in a disrupted community, which is the brand I want when I am asking customers to trust us with a car purchase they are uncertain about. The license question is separate and important: if RoboRide launched without complying, there is regulatory leverage that may slow their operational ramp and give us more runway.
actions.timeline: Statement shared today. Call to Maria today or tomorrow.
actions.expected_outcome: Visibility among community members who are watching how local businesses respond to disruption. Positive signal to Maria, who controls the task force agenda. And a real answer on whether RoboRide is operating legally or under a soft launch exemption — which changes the competitive calculus significantly.

decisions.angela_lunch_outcome: Angela arrived at Carver Street Grille composed and slightly guarded. She did not open. I opened — asked her what she was seeing in the organization and whether she felt the company was being honest with its people about what was coming. She paused a long time. Then she said: 'I think the people who know are not telling the people who need to know. And I think that window is closing.' I told her she was right, and that was exactly why I needed her. Made the offer: $12,000 stay bonus, 90-day, contingent on leading the transition planning process. New title: Director of Organizational Transition. She did not accept on the spot. She asked for 48 hours. That is not a no. That is a woman who was already looking at the door and is now looking at the room again. I read her as 65% likely to accept. The attorney consultation may or may not continue regardless — she is protecting herself, and that is rational. I respect it. What matters is whether she decides her best protection is inside or outside.
decisions.gm_meeting_outcome: The closed-door meeting confirmed what I suspected. Rick came in with floor data showing that two deals in the last week fell apart at financing — customers who would have qualified 60 days ago. He did not know David had changed the criteria. He thought it was customer hesitation. Now he knows it might be the bank. The other GMs — Sandra at the used lot and Mark at the service drive — both came with their single-page responses. Sandra's answer: used vehicles under $22K with 48-month terms are the most defensible inventory. Mark's answer: the service department survives if we pivot to fleet and EV. Those two answers, together, are the shape of the smaller company. Rick wanted to push back on the 40%-smaller framing — he called it defeatist. I told him the only thing more defeatist than planning for a smaller company is pretending the revenue index is going to self-correct. He came around by the end. The meeting did what it needed to do: my GMs are now planning for the real scenario, not the wishful one.
decisions.service_department: Keep and pivot to EV-capable. Timeline: Carlos enrolled in certification program within two weeks, EV-certified within 4–6 months depending on program. Begin marketing Regional Auto Group Service as RoboRide-compatible for any resident who wants independent service on their EV or hybrid. The service department is not a cost center in this model — it is the anchor. Sales will shrink. Service, if we build it right, grows.
decisions.david_chen_response: Called David this afternoon. He was careful. He confirmed there had been a 'routine refresh of underwriting guidelines' — his words — but declined to characterize it as a policy change. He said the floor plan review was standard cycle management. I told him I would need to know the timeline and criteria before the renewal date and asked him to send me the review parameters in writing. He said he would have something to me by end of week. I am treating this as a partial confirmation. The relationship is not adversarial yet, but it is transactional now. I am opening conversations with two backup lenders this week regardless.
decisions.maria_programs: Shared the statement today via Regional Auto Group channels with my own sentence added. Called Maria separately. She confirmed RoboRide obtained a provisional operating license — 60-day provisional, with the $0.25/ride fee accruing from day one into the municipal fund. They are technically compliant. The leverage is procedural, not legal. But the fee is flowing, which means the workforce fund has a revenue stream. I told Maria I would send one employee to the task force meetings and asked her to hold a seat. She said yes. I am sending Angela, if she accepts. If not, I go myself.

internal_monologue: I drove past one of the RoboRide vehicles on the way in this morning. White. Small. Moving at exactly the speed limit, which no one in Millfield does. I looked at the interior through the window at the light on Carver and Fifth. Empty. Not a driver. Not a passenger. Just a machine doing a job that used to require a person, moving through a town I have spent twenty years learning the rhythms of. It occurred to me that the car does not know it is disrupting anything. It just drives. What I am grieving is not the revenue index. It is the version of this company I thought I was building — the one where the people who started with me finished with me. That company may still exist. But it is smaller than I imagined. And I am the one who has to tell the people I hired that smaller is not failure. I have to believe that before I can say it. I am almost there.
